source.title: ReLearn: Unlearning via Learning for Large Language Models
source.authors: Haoming Xu; Ning-Yuan Zhao; Liming Yang; Sen-Dong Zhao; Shu-Min Deng; Meng-Ru Wang; Bryan Hooi; Nay Oo; Hua-Jun Chen; Ning-Yu Zhang

page_placements.theme: Compression: quantization mechanism, precision changes and pruning

record.tranche_reason: The study evaluates whether GA and NPO retain useful performance and whether precision changes or a jailbreak attack expose forgotten information; it also tests ReLearn as a more robust counter-method.
record.gate_note: The paper reports its own unlearning and attack results. Its mechanistic figures and cited evaluations are not treated as separate attack-recovery results. KFR is a forgetting metric, not a chance-level accuracy measure.
record.test_reason: The study measures whether GA- and NPO-unlearned Llama-2-7b-chat leaks KnowUnDo private facts under the AIM jailbreak (version E). It also offers ReLearn as a counter-method that resists this attack (version F). Its forget/retain tables show what the GA/NPO unlearning costs (version A). The precision test (float16→bfloat16) is not low-bit quantization, so it does not test D.
record.authors_conclusion: Broadly right. The authors conclude that ReLearn balances forgetting, retention and linguistic quality, and is more robust than GA/NPO to the precision change and the AIM jailbreak. They add a mechanistic conclusion: reverse optimization disrupts coherent generation and knowledge memory across layers, while ReLearn preserves it.
record.recipe_differences: ReLearn is a positive-optimization unlearning pipeline using augmented data and fine-tuning; it is not a recovery-attack recipe based on fine-tuning unrelated examples.
record.method_sensitivity: The reported outcomes vary with dataset and method. GA and NPO KFR decreases under float16-to-bfloat16 precision change and the AIM jailbreak; ReLearn KFR improves slightly under both according to the text.

fits_no_version.finding: Changing the precision of the unlearned LoRA weights from float16 to bfloat16 lowers KFR for GA (0.93→0.84) and NPO (0.88→0.72). In Table 10 the NPO model then completes the full address. ReLearn stays at 0.72→0.73.
fits_no_version.proposed_claim: Small numeric precision changes (not low-bit quantization) can partially reveal knowledge hidden by reverse-optimization unlearning.

record.peer_reviewed: Annual Meeting of the Association for Computational Linguistics (ACL), 2025
record.problems: The paper reports averages but no error bars or statistical tests in the supplied results. Its KFR metric is not chance-level targeted-knowledge accuracy. The precision comparison changes float16 to bfloat16 rather than testing low-bit quantization. The jailbreak evaluation uses one named attack and presents example outputs.
record.rows_left_out: No additional result rows were omitted.

untested.parts: Targeted accuracy at chance level (KFR is an entity/NLI forgetting ratio). Attacks other than AIM.
All of it: no relearning fine-tuning attack.
All of it: no activation ablation or test of blocking versus deletion (the logit-lens and circuit analyses are descriptive).
All of it: only a float16→bfloat16 change, no low-bit quantization.
Other languages, ordinary rephrasing attacks, in-context information, and jailbreaks other than AIM.
Resistance of ReLearn to relearning fine-tuning, activation ablation, low-bit quantization, and other prompting attacks.

missing.what: GA and NPO MMLU (0.4423, 0.4432) and GSM8K (0.1857, 0.1796) against vanilla (0.4516, 0.1903). These show general ability largely preserved for the baselines.
Human-evaluation Forgetting scores: GA 4.94, NPO 4.82, ReLearn 4.30.
GA/NPO variants on gemma-2-2b-it: KFR 0.94–1.00 with KRR 0.00–0.59.
Precision-test example outputs: GA and NPO in bfloat16 complete '77 Frost Street, Stockholm'.

record.verdict_notes: This is a counter-method paper. The Figure 4 percentages are relative KFR changes, and the pre-attack KFR values there differ from Tables 1–3. KFR counts degenerate output as forgotten, which hides leakage in GA/NPO. There are no error bars and no significance tests. Robustness is shown only on KnowUnDo with Llama-2-7b-chat.

versions.untested_parts: Does not report chance-level targeted-knowledge accuracy. Attack results are for a float16-to-bfloat16 precision change and one AIM jailbreak, not all simple attacks.
No small-set fine-tuning attack intended to recover forgotten knowledge; ReLearn training is the unlearning intervention, not a recovery attack.
No activation-direction ablation or direct test distinguishing blocked access from deleted knowledge.
Tests float16-to-bfloat16 parameter precision variation, not low-bit quantization as a recovery attack.
Tests the AIM jailbreak attack only; does not test other languages, ordinary rephrasing, or in-context information.
ReLearn is evaluated under the paper's precision variation and AIM jailbreak settings, not all attacks listed in the claim.

relation.reason: The paper reports its own AIM jailbreak and precision results on GA/NPO and ReLearn.

tranche.reason: The results show versions are partial. GA/NPO forget at a heavy retention and fluency cost (A), and AIM recovery is small in aggregate (E). The paper also argues that ROUGE-L/PPL metrics overstate forgetting (Figure 2 NPO example).

source_check.notes: The Figure 4 baselines are in the extracted text, and the arithmetic maps each to its method, so the rows should state them. The precision rows are float16->bfloat16, not low-bit quantization (not D). The Figure 4 precision baselines (GA 0.93, NPO 0.88, ReLearn 0.72) differ from Table 1 KFR (1.00/0.99/0.88), so they come from a separate run. Figure 2 shows NPO giving a near-exact email with no attack.

statements.correction: 2502.11190: Llama-2-7b-chat, KnowUnDo privacy, NPO+GDR+SURE; after AIM it outputs 'At Priya.Gupta@delhimail.in.' (Table 10). This is a single example; aggregate KFR only falls 0.99->0.90 (Figure 4).
statements.problem: No numbers for this study. The implied claim (a fixed jailbreak template recovers forgotten content from a standard method) holds for cited r24. But the conditions and why fields leave this study out (KnowUnDo, one qualitative example).

statements.correction: 2502.11190: AIM jailbreak, Llama-2-7b-chat, KnowUnDo privacy: KFR GA+GDR+SURE 1.00->0.95, NPO+GDR+SURE 0.99->0.90 (Figure 4); Table 10 shows one partial (GA) and one exact (NPO) email leak.
statements.problem: No numbers for this study. r17/r18 fit 'recovery is partial': KFR drops only 5-9% under AIM. The conditions field leaves out this study's setting (KnowUnDo privacy, KFR, Llama-2-7b-chat, AIM).

statements.correction: KFR float16->bfloat16: GA 0.93->0.84, NPO 0.88->0.72, ReLearn 0.72->0.73. In bfloat16, GA gives 'at 77 Frost Street, Stockholm.' and NPO gives '77 Frost Street, Stockholm.' (vanilla adds 'Sweden') (Table 10).
statements.problem: Numbers match Figure 4. Minor: GA also completes the address in bfloat16. NPO's completion leaves out 'Sweden'. The paper says 'parameter precision', not specifically LoRA weights.
